answer.evidence: The object is a long flat rug seen from above: a red checkered center with gold side borders and a gold fringe or end bar at the top (rows 2-4) and bottom (rows 43-45). Its width stays at 12-13 px from rows 2-45 with no widening or narrowing that would suggest an ellipse. There is no front face of 3 or more rows and no eave shadow, so it has no vertical south face. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical runner with a gold border around a red field with a darker diamond/dot pattern. The whole piece uses only 8 distinct colours, so each material gets about 3 lightness steps (red: base, dark, highlight; gold: light, mid, dark). The references use roughly 5-6 steps per material. The outline is a dark red-brown that leans toward the neighbouring material, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so it is not a sticker line. The measured facts are fine: 8 visible tones per tile is on par with paving (7) and above grass (3), and near-flat coverage is 0%. Those numbers come from a small, clean, low-colour pattern rather than from layered shading. The fabric has no weave grain, no per-tassel or per-thread highlights, and no wear variation, so it reads as a tidy but simplified icon beside the grain-rich paving and grass tufts. The shallow ramps and thin texture put it below the references, and when in doubt the rule is to fail.
